description: Grain is transported from a farm to local grocery stores in either large bags or tiny bags. Large bags can hold 25 kg of grain and requires 4 units of energy to transport. Tiny bags can hold 6 kg of grain and requires 1.5 units of energy to transport. The distribution process has access to 110 units of energy. Because of popularity of buying in bulk, there must be twice as many large bags as tiny bags of rice. Additionally, there must be at least 20 tiny bags of rice. How many of each size of rice bags should be used to maximize the total amount of grain in weight?

LargeBagCapacity.definition: The capacity of a large bag in kilograms

LargeBagEnergy.definition: The energy required to transport a large bag

TinyBagCapacity.definition: The capacity of a tiny bag in kilograms

TinyBagEnergy.definition: The energy required to transport a tiny bag

RatioLargeToTiny.definition: The ratio of large bags to tiny bags

MinTinyBags.definition: Minimum number of tiny bags required

objective.description: "Maximize the total amount of grain transported (in kilograms) using large and tiny bags"

constraints.description: 4 * (number of large bags) + 1.5 * (number of tiny bags) must be less than or equal to 110
The number of large bags must be equal to 2 times the number of tiny bags
The number of tiny bags must be at least 20
The number of large bags and tiny bags must be integers
